title: The Goldilocks Principle of Drain Pipe Slope
description: Maintaining correct slope is crucial for gravity drainage systems. A common mistake during rough-in installation is assuming steeper pipe pitch equals better drainage. If a horizontal drain line has too much slope, water flows out too quickly, leaving solid waste behind to accumulate and cause blockages. Conversely, insufficient slope leads to standing water and sluggish flow, causing heavy debris to settle in the pipe. Standard plumbing code generally recommends a 1/4-inch fall per linear foot for pipes up to 3 inches in diameter, balancing liquid velocity and solid transport. Always check local plumbing codes for specific slope requirements based on pipe diameter.
